question.problem:
A cinema admission fee is normally distributed with a mean of $\mu $ dollars and a standard deviation of $\$0.75.$ Additionally, in $94%$ of cases the admission fee is between $\$0.7\mu $ and $\$1.3\mu .$ Find the percentage of cases when the admission fee is lower than $\$5.$

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $p$ | $\,0.75\,$ | $\,0.80\,$ | $\,0.85\,$ | $\,0.90\,$ | $\,0.95\,$ | $\,0.97\,$ | $\,0.99\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ | $\,1.8808\,$ | $\,2.3263\,$ |

$$

$$

*In addition, you're given the following table of values for $p=Φ(z)$*.

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.4\,$ | $\,0.6554\,$ | $\,0.6591\,$ | $\,0.6628\,$ |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.6915\,$ | $\,0.6950\,$ | $\,0.6985\,$ |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7257\,$ | $\,0.7291\,$ | $\,0.7324\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent a randomly selected admission fee. Then we have $X∼N(\mu ,{0.75}^{2}),$ and we want to find $P(X<5).$ But first, we need to find the mean $\mu .$ 

We know that $P(0.7\mu <X<1.3\mu )=0.94.$ First, we convert this to a cumulative probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.7\mu <X<1.3\mu ) & =0.94 \\ 2P(\mu <X<1.3\mu ) & =0.94 \\ P(\mu <X<1.3\mu ) & =0.47 \\ P(X<\mu )+P(\mu <X<1.3\mu ) & =0.5+0.47 \\ P(X<1.3\mu ) & =0.97\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<1.3\mu ) & =0.97 \\ P(Z<\frac{0.3\mu }{0.75}) & =0.97 \\ Φ(\frac{0.3\mu }{0.75}) & =0.97 \\ \frac{0.3\mu }{0.75} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.97) \\ 0.4\mu  & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.97).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.97)≈1.8808.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}0.4\mu  & =1.8808 \\ \mu  & =\frac{1.8808}{0.4} \\  & ≈4.702.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we can solve for $P(X<5)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<5) & =P(Z<\frac{5-4.702.}{0.75}) \\  & ≈P(Z<0.40) \\  & =Φ(0.40) \\  & =0.6554 \\  & ≈65.5%\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, approximately in $65.5%$ of cases, the admission fee is lower than $\$5.$
